canDo: Can link short sentences with qui/que/où, and begin handling dont for de + antecedent.
review: Review qui/que/où; learn the de relation of dont, and get to know common compound relative pronouns.
input: Listening: introducing people/places; reading: a cultural profile.
output: Write a 120-word profile of a person or place; speak for 2 minutes using ≥5 relative clauses.
checkpoint: ≥80% on mixed qui/que/où questions; can spot the de relation behind dont.
challenge: Today’s challenge: choose a French-speaking singer, writer or athlete you admire and write 5 sentences about them, each linked with qui, que or où (e.g. C’est une chanteuse que j’écoute souvent); you can look them up first on TV5MONDE Apprendre or RFI.

questions.why: « que l'on peut emprunter gratuitement, et qu'elle ne vend pas ». These aren’t books that don’t sell, but books she finds hard to recommend in a few words.
« que je n'arrive pas à conseiller en trois phrases » — they need a conversation to explain.
« plutôt que de construire des logements neufs, elle a racheté et rénové huit maisons vides ». The reopened classroom is a result.
« Reste une difficulté … : les emplois ». The broadband work was finished last year — a condition that has been met, not the current difficulty.
« des photographies que les clients n'ont jamais récupérées ». 1979 is the year the studio closed.
« C'est la décision qui a sauvé la journée » refers to moving the workshops under the halle. The stage was cancelled, not moved.
« ne pouvait pas être montée sur un sol détrempé ». The rain had stopped by mid-afternoon.
« cherche depuis deux ans un local où stocker son matériel »; forty is the current number of volunteers.
Aerial photos taken in a drought showed the grass yellowing faster above the old paths. No seeds survived.
« chaque allée correspond à un tracé retrouvé »; the eighteenth-century lists were used to choose the plants, not the paths.
The plants were chosen by the gardeners from historical lists — a choice made in the reconstruction.
Tapes of field recordings from the seventies: elderly singers, often unaccompanied.
« ces chanteurs eux-mêmes transformaient ce qu'ils avaient appris ». She keeps the melody but adds modern arrangements.
« Ce qui a changé les choses, c'est l'arrivée du tramway en 2010 ». The shops closed first and only came back later with the people.
« à tarif réduit pour les personnes âgées et les étudiants »; three screenings a week is the total.

V13-05.exZh: This is the narrow street where she settled eight years ago.

V13-06.exZh: The bookshop is also a place where you can borrow books for free.

V13-07.exZh: Hélène Vasseur runs a forty-square-metre bookshop.

V13-08.exZh: These are books I can’t manage to recommend in three sentences.

V13-09.exZh: Some end up buying the book, others don’t, and I don’t mind.

V13-10.exZh: The village renovated eight empty houses, which it rents to families at a moderate rent.

V13-11.exZh: Rather than building new housing, the town hall renovated empty houses.

V13-12.exZh: The village rents these houses to families at a moderate rent.

V13-13.exZh: Most of the adults who moved here work remotely.

V13-14.exZh: The village is located a thousand metres above sea level.

V13-15.exZh: These portraits come from a neighbourhood studio that closed in 1979.

V13-16.exZh: It’s precisely this emptiness that the exhibition puts on stage.

V13-17.exZh: Nothing indicates who these people are.

V13-18.exZh: The Washhouse Festival is held every year on the first Sunday in October.

V13-19.exZh: The festival drew nearly two thousand people despite the rain.

V13-20.exZh: The organisers cancelled the evening concert because the ground was waterlogged.

V13-21.exZh: The Saint-Amand cinema will reopen its doors on 4 April.

V13-22.exZh: What I take away from this visit is the emotion the anonymous portraits stir up.

V13-23.exZh: On Tuesday afternoons, there’s a screening at a reduced rate.

V13-24.exZh: It was an aerial photograph that set everything off.

V13-25.exZh: The plants were chosen based on eighteenth-century lists.

V13-26.exZh: Some people criticise me for betraying tradition.

V13-27.zh: to be at the heart of …
V13-27.exZh: The melody, which is at the heart of these songs, doesn’t change.

V13-28.exZh: The media library has all the recordings I need.

V13-29.zh: What I like about someone is …
V13-29.exZh: What I like about her is her curiosity.

V13-30.exZh: What I like about this village is the peace and quiet.

V13-31.exZh: I’d like to know whether the museum offers visits for groups.

V13-32.exZh: The museum runs a guided tour every Sunday at 15:00.

V13-33.exZh: The two shows overlap: I can’t see both.

V13-34.exZh: Access is free; you just have to register.

V13-35.exZh: After the factory closed, the neighbourhood emptied.

V13-36.exZh: The shops closed one after another.

V13-37.exZh: Before opening her bookshop, she worked in publishing for a long time.

V13-38.exZh: These modern arrangements sometimes earn me criticism.

V13-39.exZh: The exhibition showcases the work of a forgotten photographer.

V13-40.exZh: At the festival, I met a fascinating musician.

V13-41.exZh: Volunteers introduce visitors to the local heritage.

V13-42.exZh: This village is known for its Washhouse Festival.

V13-43.exZh: My uncle, who is passionate about photography, visited the exhibition three times.

V13-44.exZh: Since she retired, my mother has done voluntary work for a cultural association.
